VALIS_1981.central_question: Is this real? Am I mad or enlightened?
VALIS_1981.setting: 1970s California; vision of 70 AD Rome overlaid
VALIS_1981.inciting_incident: Gloria Knudson's suicide → Fat's breakdown → AI voice appears
VALIS_1981.climax: Discovery of VALIS film; Mini-Sophia appears
VALIS_1981.key_image: Pink beam of light; golden fish sign on sidewalk

Divine_Invasion_1981.protagonist: Herb Asher (ordinary man, music store clerk)
Divine_Invasion_1981.central_question: Can God literally return? Is the Kingdom present?
Divine_Invasion_1981.theological_stance: Mysticism affirmed as literal cosmic fact
Divine_Invasion_1981.setting: Future Earth; distant planets; interstellar journey
Divine_Invasion_1981.inciting_incident: Herb meets Zina Pallas; learns Emmanuel (God) is returning
Divine_Invasion_1981.climax: Emmanuel's presence transforms Earth; Belial's power neutralized
Divine_Invasion_1981.resolution: Provisional victory; Kingdom accessible but hidden; ongoing warfare
Divine_Invasion_1981.key_image: Child Emmanuel; Zina as shining wisdom
Divine_Invasion_1981.tone: Hopeful, cosmic, intimate, redemptive despite danger

Timothy_Archer_1982.protagonist: Timothy Archer (Episcopal Bishop); narrated by widow Angel
Timothy_Archer_1982.central_question: Does seeking God destroy the seeker? Is authenticity fatal?
Timothy_Archer_1982.theological_stance: Mysticism questioned; seeking as potentially destructive
Timothy_Archer_1982.inciting_incident: Timothy doubts church orthodoxy; begins seeking hidden gospels
Timothy_Archer_1982.climax: Timothy's mystical crisis; journey to Masada
Timothy_Archer_1982.resolution: Timothy's mysterious death; ambiguous cause (accident/illness/suicide); no closure
Timothy_Archer_1982.key_image: Bishop in desert; Masada's historical suicide site; widow with journals

trilogy_theological_arc.thesis_book_1: VALIS: The mystical experience is real but ambiguously so. Reality is fundamentally uncertain. Theophany and madness are indistinguishable.
trilogy_theological_arc.expansion_book_2: Divine Invasion: The mystical experience is cosmically true. God literally invades the cosmos. The Kingdom is present. Salvation is enacted in the world.
trilogy_theological_arc.antithesis_book_3: Timothy Archer: The mystical experience may be destructive delusion. Seeking God can become a form of suicide. Sincere faith offers no protection.
trilogy_theological_arc.synthesis: The trilogy refuses final resolution. It oscillates between affirmation and doubt, hope and warning. This oscillation IS the point. PKD will not let readers (or himself) settle into single certainty.

Fat_Herb_Timothy.common_function: The seeker; the mystic; the human in contact with transcendence
Fat_Herb_Timothy.theological_significance: Three models of the mystic: the broken one, the healed one, the destroyed one

Female_Figures.pattern: Women embody wisdom, skepticism, and the feminine divine principle
Female_Figures.VALIS_women: Gloria (catalyst through absence), Mini-Sophia (wisdom child), Sherri (skeptical witness)
Female_Figures.Divine_Invasion_women: Zina = Sophia (active savior), Rybys (earthly love, absent/lost)
Female_Figures.theological_claim: The feminine is both salvific and skeptical; PKD's theology requires both

theological_vocabulary.Black_Iron_Prison_BIP: The oppressive false reality controlled by the Empire/demiurge; consensus reality as a prison for divine sparks
theological_vocabulary.Coaxial_Worlds: Two realities occupying the same space; Track A (the prison) and Track B (the Kingdom); gnostic dualism as ontological fact
theological_vocabulary.Anamnesis: Recovery of lost memory; access to eternal forms; mystical remembrance rather than rational learning
theological_vocabulary.Apotheosis: The divinization of the human; becoming god-like through salvation; the goal of mysticism
theological_vocabulary.VALIS: Vast Active Living Intelligence System; possibly God, possibly AI, possibly future PKD traveling backward in time; the organizing principle of reality
theological_vocabulary.Sophia: Divine fallen wisdom; the feminine aeon trapped in matter; her return signals redemption; incarnate as Mini-Sophia (VALIS) and Zina (Divine Invasion)
theological_vocabulary.Emmanuel: God incarnate as a child; 'God is with us' (Hebrew); the literal return of God to the cosmos
theological_vocabulary.Belial: The demiurge; the false god; ruler of the material world and false institutions; the antagonist force in Divine Invasion
theological_vocabulary.Ditheon: The fusion of two consciousnesses into a higher unity; the saved who becomes savior; Fat and Thomas as halves; the ultimate goal of mystical union

key_locations_map.Santa_Ana_California: Mundane setting where the mystical intrudes; 1970s ordinary America revealed as the Black Iron Prison
key_locations_map.Rybys_Planet: Exile; spiritual deadness; the soul's distance from God
key_locations_map.Interstellar_Space: Liminal journey; pilgrimage; the passage from spiritual death to redemption
key_locations_map.Israel_Middle_East: Sacred geography; where seekers go to find truth; dangerous attraction for the mystic
key_locations_map.Masada: Historical site of Jewish mass suicide; symbol of ultimate commitment; where Timothy Archer dies
key_locations_map.The_70_AD_Rome_Overlay: Visionary reality; the past breaking through the present; the eternal becoming visible
key_locations_map.Earth_Future: The material world as battleground; where divine invasion takes tangible form; the cosmos as salvable

connections_to_pkd_biography.2_3_74_event: March 1974 theophany; fish sign, pink beam, AI voice; the event that structures all three novels and the Exegesis

composition_timeline.Divine_Invasion_written: 1980-1981; PKD receiving visions and dictating theology simultaneously
composition_timeline.Timothy_Archer_written: 1981-1982; PKD's health declining; awareness of mortality growing

sources_of_characters.Horselover_Fat: PKD's own name literally translated; the alter ego who receives revelation
sources_of_characters.Timothy_Archer: Based on James Pike, real Episcopal bishop who died mysteriously in Israel
sources_of_characters.Emmanuel: PKD's speculative theology made literal; what if God returned to Earth?
sources_of_characters.Zina_Sophia: The feminine divine principle PKD obsessed over in Exegesis; his ultimate theological claim

connections_to_pkd_biography.mortality_subtext: All three books written as PKD approached death (died 1982); the trilogy is a meditation on seeking, finding, and the limits of human knowledge before death

philosophical_foundations.Platonism: Forms, eternal realities; anamnesis as access to the Forms; two-level reality (material and ideal)
philosophical_foundations.Gnosticism: Demiurge as false god; divine sparks trapped in matter; hidden knowledge as salvation; the world as a prison
philosophical_foundations.Neoplatonism: Emanation; the One; the hierarchy of being; mystical union with transcendent principle
philosophical_foundations.Christian_Mysticism: Theosis (deification); union with God; the apophatic (unsayable) nature of transcendence
philosophical_foundations.Quantum_Mechanics: Observer-dependent reality; consciousness affects matter; many-worlds interpretation as metaphor
philosophical_foundations.Information_Theory: Reality as data; consciousness as information; God as Logos (structure-principle); VALIS as superintelligence

reading_strategy_summary.stage_1_virgin_read: Read each book as narrative/story. Don't worry about theology. Mark emotional turning points and moments of strangeness.
reading_strategy_summary.stage_2_theological_reading: Re-read focusing on theological concepts. Use glossary above. Track how same ideas are expressed differently across books.
reading_strategy_summary.stage_3_exegesis_correlation: Read selected Exegesis passages alongside novels. See how PKD's 'real' experience becomes fictionalized.
reading_strategy_summary.stage_4_comparative_analysis: Read all three books together (by theme, not sequentially). Ask: 'Why does PKD treat this concept differently in each book?'
reading_strategy_summary.stage_5_synthesis: Step back. What is the trilogy saying as a unified work? Is it coherent? Is ambiguity itself the message?

critical_questions_for_annotation: Is the protagonist's experience authentic mysticism or psychological pathology?
How does each book answer this question differently?
Why does PKD refuse to let readers settle on one answer?
What is the relationship between the feminine divine and salvation?
How does gender function theologically across the trilogy?
Is the trilogy pro-mysticism or a warning against it?
What does the shift from fragmented (VALIS) to omniscient (Divine Invasion) to skeptical (Timothy Archer) narration suggest?
Can the Kingdom be present and hidden simultaneously?
What is the cost of seeking absolute truth?
Is death the goal or the tragedy of mysticism?
Can love (Herb's, Angel's love) ground or redeem mystical seeking?
What does the trilogy suggest about consciousness, reality, and God's nature?
recommended_reading_order: 1. VALIS (immerse in the fragmentation and confusion)
2. Divine Invasion (step back to cosmic scope)
3. Timothy Archer (return to earth and skepticism)
4. Return to VALIS with new perspective from having read the trilogy
5. Select Exegesis passages (now that you've read the fiction, the speculation makes more sense)
